issues.legal_issue: A statutory remedy limited to decrees for recovery of possession does not extend to a summary order for possession made in a proceeding that is not a suit.
material_facts: The landlord began summary proceedings to recover possession under the procedure for recovery of immovable property before the Small Cause Court.
The court made an order directing delivery of possession, and the tenants later sought to have that order vacated under a statutory provision offering relief against specified possession decrees.
The tenants had not yet lost possession, but the possession order arose from a summary proceeding rather than a suit resulting in a decree.
issues.conclusion: The statutory remedy did not apply to the possession order, and the tenants were not entitled to relief under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: The court read section 18(1) of the West Bengal Premises Rent Control (Temporary Provisions) Act, 1950, in light of the 1948 Act to which it referred. Sections 11 and 12 of the 1948 Act distinguish an order from a decree and a proceeding from a suit; section 11’s reference to the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act recognizes possession orders under sections 41 and 43 of that Act separately from decrees. The court also applied the ordinary meaning of “decree” as a formal adjudication in a suit, as defined in the Code of Civil Procedure. It rejected the contrary construction in Rai Bahadur Atulya Dhan Banerjee v. Sudhangsu Bhusan Dutta and the decisions following it, including Dhanesh Prokash Pal v. Lalit Mohan Ghosh, Mohan Lal Khettry v. Chuni Lal Khettry, Jethmull Sethia v. Aloke Ganguly, and Iswari Prosad Goenka v. N. B. Sen; it referred to Rai Meherbai Sorabji Master v. Pherozshaw Sorabji Gazdar on the character of a possession order under the summary procedure.

rule.if: summary_possession_proceeding and possession_order_instead_of_suit_decree and relief_text_limited_to_decrees and tenant_still_in_possession and tenant_sought_relief

predicates.summary_possession_proceeding: A landlord sought recovery of premises through a summary possession proceeding rather than an ordinary suit.
predicates.possession_order_instead_of_suit_decree: The proceeding resulted in an order for possession rather than a decree made in a suit.
predicates.relief_text_limited_to_decrees: The statutory relief sought was expressed to apply to possession decrees, without including possession orders.
predicates.tenant_still_in_possession: The tenant had not yet surrendered or otherwise lost possession when relief was sought.
predicates.tenant_sought_relief: The tenant applied to have the possession outcome set aside under the statutory relief provision.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks statutory relief while still in possession after a summary proceeding has produced a possession order, and the relief text covers decrees only, the relief is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot enlarge clear statutory language to remedy an assumed legislative mistake or omission, even where the resulting distinction appears unfair.
material_facts: The statutory text granted relief in terms of decrees for possession and did not include the distinct summary orders at issue.
The tenants argued that a narrow reading would deny relief to some tenants while granting it to others, contrary to the legislature’s presumed intention.
The court concluded that the text was clear and that any deficiency in the legislation was for the legislature, not the court, to remedy.
issues.conclusion: The court could not extend the statutory relief to cover the omitted category of possession orders on the assumption that the legislature had made a mistake.
issues.legal_principle: In construing a statute, a court must proceed on the basis that the legislature intended what it enacted and may not add to or amend clear language to correct defective phrasing or fill a casus omissus. The court relied on Commissioner for Special Purposes of Income Tax v. Pemsel, Crawford v. Spooner, and Hansraj Gupta v. Official Liquidator of Dehra Dun-Mussoorie Electric Tramway Co. Ltd.

rule.if: statutory_interpretation_case and text_names_a_limited_category and claimed_legislative_omission and argument_seeks_extension_beyond_text

predicates.statutory_interpretation_case: A court is deciding the scope of a statutory remedy in a proceeding about that remedy.
predicates.text_names_a_limited_category: The statutory text identifies a limited category of outcomes to which the remedy applies.
predicates.claimed_legislative_omission: A party argues that the legislature left out another category that should have been included.
predicates.argument_seeks_extension_beyond_text: A party asks the court to extend the remedy beyond the category stated in the text.

issues.definition: When a party seeks to extend a remedy beyond a limited category stated in the text to cure an asserted omission, the court must not make that extension.
